messages:
lee: heads-up: after the mdx migration a few deep links under /guides/runtime now jump to the wrong spot — linkcheck showed several collisions where two headings got the same slug.

olivia: I think this is because some headings include an inline code span now (`<Component>`) which the new slugger normalizes differently than the old one.

lee: exact repro: `## Using <Runtime> in production` and `## Using Runtime in production` both became `using-runtime-in-production`. mkdocs then only kept the first id, so anchors to the second are 404s.

link-bot: linkcheck: /guides/runtime#using-runtime-in-production -> 200 but /guides/runtime#using-runtime-in-production-1 -> 404 (expected)

olivia: options: 1) change content to avoid inline code in headings (not ideal), 2) use explicit header IDs (`## Heading {#custom-id}`), 3) change slugger to include punctuation tokens so code vs plain produce different slugs.

lee: I prefer option 3 for backward-compatibility. quick patch: switch the slugify function to preserve angle brackets when present by replacing `<>` with `-angle-` before slugify. risky but minimal.

olivia: can we instead implement a deterministic de-dup scheme that appends a suffix only when collisions happen (like -1) but also emits both ids (the duplicate plus the suffixed) so links written to either still work?

lee: implemented a small plugin that post-processes the HTML and ensures duplicate ids are canonicalized: first occurrence keeps plain slug, subsequent ones get `-n` suffix, and we add a data-attr `data-original-id` with the computed original so old links can be redirected by JS. opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4412

ci-bot: docs build triggered for PR 4412. linkcheck will run after build.

link-bot: after applying plugin on the built site, duplicate anchors resolved; linkcheck now reports only a couple other unrelated 404s.

olivia: tested locally; plugin preserves both headers and makes links to older slug patterns work via small client-side redirect snippet. added unit test for header collision.

lee: merged after CI green. follow-up: audit headings across the site for other collisions and add a lint rule to warn on headings whose slugify(normalized) collides with an existing slug.

olivia: filed issue #802 to add the heading collision linter.

lee: closing thread. thanks.
